newsitem.title: USA: Police get autopsy report on JonBenet's sister.
newsitem.headline: Police get autopsy report on JonBenet's sister.

text.p: Boulder police are looking at the autopsy report on the older half-sister of JonBenet Ramsey, the 6-year-old beauty pageant winner who was murdered in December, an official said Thursday.
"The 1992 autopsy report (on JonBenet's sister) is now part of our file," police spokesman Kelvin McNeill told a briefing. He declined to say why the autopsy was being examined.
Elizabeth Ramsey was killed in a car accident near Chicago in 1992. She was 22 years old at the time of her death.

"As of this morning our investigators are not in Chicago and have not been to Chicago," McNeill said. But he said several members of the Boulder police force were out of state at an undisclosed location.

JonBenet's body was found on Dec. 26 by her father, John Ramsey, in a windowless room in the basement of the family's home in Boulder. Eight hours earlier her mother, Patricia Ramsey, said she had found a ransom note demanding $118,000.

McNeill said DNA samples were still being prepared to be sent to Cellmark Laboratory in Maryland where additional work would be done. Police have conducted more than 115 interviews in Colorado and other states during the 10-week investigation but no suspects have been named and no arrests have been made.
"We have not ruled anybody in or out as a suspect," McNeill said.

Boulder police were in Roswell, Georgia, last weekend. The Ramseys lived in Georgia before moving to Colorado in 1991. McNeill declined to disclose who had been interviewed other than to say that police had no contact with JonBenet's parents.
The Ramseys, with their 10-year-old son Burke, returned to the Denver area on Monday.
